questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Work done
options: can either be positive or negative
questions.solution:
Work done by a constant force is given as
\(W=F s \cos $\theta$\)
where, \(F=\) applied force
\(s=\) displacement
and \(\theta=$\) angle between the direction of force and displacement.
When, \(\theta=$0^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}\), then \(W=F s\) (positive)
When, \(\theta=$90^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}\), then \(W=F s \cos 90^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}\)
\(=0 \text { (zero) }\)
When, \(\theta=$180^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}\), then \(W=F s \cos 180^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}\)
\(=-F s $\text { (negative) }$\)
Hence, work done may be positive, negative or zero.

questions.solution:
Given, \(P=7 $\mathrm{~W}$\), mass, \(m=15 $\mathrm{~kg}$\),
\(v_i=3 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-1} \text { and }$v_f=5 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$\)
From work-energy theorem,
\(\begin{array}{rlrl} & $\text { Work done }$& $=\frac{1}{2}m\left($v_f^2-v_i^2\right) \\
& \Rightarrow & & $=\frac{1}{2} \times$15(25-9) \\
& \Rightarrow & W & =120 $\mathrm{~J}
\end{array}$\)
So, the time of work done,
\$(t=\frac{\text { work }}{\text { power }}=\frac{120}{7}=$1714 $\mathrm{~s}$\)
Hence, the acceleration,
\$(a=\frac{v_f-v_i}{t}=\frac{5-3}{17.14}=$0.116 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}^2\)
Distance travelled by car,
\$(D=\frac{v_f^2-v_i^2}{2 a}=\frac{5^2-3^2}{2 \times 0.116}=$68.96 \approx 70 $\mathrm{~m}$\)
Hence, the correct option is (d).

Rate of increase of kinetic energy
